chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Shall I brand the sheep on their faces?' He said: 'Brand them on their ears.'

key_terms.آذَان: Ears (plural of أذن), the prescribed location for branding livestock
key_terms.سِمَة: Branding mark, a hot-iron mark used to identify livestock ownership
key_terms.وُجُوه: Faces (plural of وجه), here referring to the faces of animals

ai.seo_question: Where did Imam al-Sadiq say livestock should be branded according to Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a direct exchange between Yunus ibn Ya'qub and Imam al-Sadiq (AS) regarding the permissible location for branding livestock. When asked whether sheep could be branded on their faces, the Imam directed that branding should be done on their ears instead. This ruling reflects Islamic concern for animal welfare, as the face is a sensitive area that would cause greater suffering, while the ear is a less sensitive location and a recognized conventional place for livestock marking.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus Bin Yaqoub who said,
‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Can I brand the sheep in their faces?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Brand them in their ears’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from Yunus ibn Ya’qub who has said the following: “
I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about if I can mark sheep on their faces. He (the Imam) said, ‘Mark them on their ears.’”
